why: A (universes 0; milnorCurvature, nomizuCurvature (abstract Mathlib CovariantDerivative, any model), curvature (embedded) are definitions; B's curv/nomizuCurv are definitionally A's): Nomizu's R = −Milnor's R and R(Y,X)Z = −R(X,Y)Z, for all fields. B: for a smooth connection on an ℝⁿ-manifold and smooth fields, (i) Nomizu = −Milnor; (ii) for the chart coordinate fields of extChartAt p, on its source, R(∂ᵢ,∂ⱼ)Z = −∂ᵢ⊢(∂ⱼ⊢Z) + ∂ⱼ⊢(∂ᵢ⊢Z). Both statements are theorems: A_to_B uses A's milnorCurvature_eq_neg for (i) and proves (ii) outright (B_part_ii: [∂ᵢ,∂ⱼ] = 0 on the chart source, since ∂ᵢ is locally Mathlib's mpullback of a constant field by the chart and mpullback_mlieBracket gives naturality of the bracket; then cov Z x 0 = 0); B_to_A re-proves A by abel and mlieBracket_swap without using B. So the 'equivalence' is vacuous in both directions as far as (ii) and A are concerned: B's (ii) (coordinate-field formula) is content A lacks, and A's swap identity, arbitrary models and non-smooth fields are content B lacks.
